headline: Blackstone expects Anthropic to receive a high junk rating after IPO, FT says
body: The Financial Times says Blackstone told investors in a $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips that it expects a “high” junk rating after the IPO. The FT notes that Blackstone had earlier said the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating before 2027. Anthropic and Blackstone both declined to comment to TechCrunch.

evidence.text: Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times.

The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO.
Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around.
TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment.

Blackstone’s forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business.
The lab has been on a spending spree, racking up large compute power deals throughout the past 12 months, which has worried investors .
